# Lakkhaṇa Saṁyutta (SN 19)

**ID:** SN 19  
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Lakkhaṇa Saṁyutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0302m.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0302m.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Lakkhaṇa Saṁyutta* (SN 19) is a section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya* comprising discourses set around encounters between the monks Lakkhaṇa and Mahāmoggallāna [Hazra 1994]. While descending the mountain or walking for alms, Lakkhaṇa observes Moggallāna smile and questions him as to the reason [Asanga 2016; Hazra 1994]. In the presence of the Buddha and the monastic community, Moggallāna recounts that through his psychic powers he witnessed various disembodied apparitions or spirits (*peta*s) suffering agonizing torments in the sky [Tan 2002; Hazra 1994]. The Buddha confirms having seen the same apparitions during his own awakening and explains the precise karmic actions in their past lives that led to these retributions [Tan 2002; Anālayo 2017].
